name: ShipStation
description: ShipStation shipments become Order Shipped events on the order's customer, once per shipment, with the carrier, service, tracking number and ship date. ShipStation's webhooks only point at a batch of shipments, so DumbMail fetches them, and each shipped order, with your ShipStation API key. Customers are held back from marketing: a shipment isn't consent.

credentials.name: api_key
credentials.label: ShipStation API key
credentials.help: ShipStation → Settings → Account → API Settings. Used, with the secret, to fetch the shipments and orders a webhook points to.

setup: Create the integration from this recipe and copy its webhook URL. Keep it private: ShipStation doesn't sign webhooks, so the URL is the secret.
In ShipStation, open Settings → Account → API Settings and save the API key and secret as the credentials api_key and api_secret.

In ShipStation, open Settings → Integrations → Integration Partners → Webhooks (or Settings → Account → Webhooks), add a webhook for On Items Shipped (SHIP_NOTIFY) with the webhook URL, for all stores or one store, and save.
Create a label for a test order and check the delivery log: the webhook is followed by a fetch of the batch's shipments, then of each order.
Review the draft shipping flow and turn it on. It's a service message about the customer's own order, so it reaches people held back from marketing.
ShipStation allows 40 API requests a minute. A large batch is read a page at a time; when ShipStation says to wait, DumbMail waits for the time it gives.
Addresses, items and labels are never stored: only the fields the recipe reads are kept.

flows.name: ShipStation: order shipped
flows.description: When a shipment's label is created, tells the customer their order is on its way, with the carrier and tracking number. A service message about their own order.
